clue.text: A sign of having no occupation

definitions.text: A sign of having no occupation

parts.words: A sign of having no occupation
parts.note: reads like a comment on someone out of work, but describes the notice put up on an empty flat or shop awaiting a tenant

explanation.surface: Something that shows a person is unemployed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupation' looks like a job; here it means a building being occupied, and the sign is the one advertising a property for rent.
explanation.definitionFit: The notice in the window of an untenanted property invites someone to rent it, so it signals no occupant.

clue.text: A second source found, too

parts.note: a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: Another place of supply has been discovered in addition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean also or in addition.

clue.text: A lovable disposition may be most important

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters of the preceding words are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A sweet nature may matter more than anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposition' pretends to mean temperament but is the anagram signal: A LOVABLE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to single out the thing that matters more than anything else, i.e. chiefly.

clue.text: Continue to flirt?

definitions.meaning: to have a flirtation or affair with them

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means keep going, and also, informally, conduct a dalliance with someone.

clue.text: Question about the way speech is reported

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the word question are moved around

explanation.surface: Asking something concerning how people's words are relayed in print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning' but asks for QUESTION to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Direct speech in writing is set between inverted commas, so the words appear within quotation marks.

clue.text: Players with one way out — strike

parts.note: the actors in a play are its cast
I is the Roman numeral for one
a gate is a way out of a field or garden

explanation.surface: Actors, finding a single exit, hit someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise or punish severely, originally by beating, is close in sense to hitting someone.

clue.text: Quarters provided by the bank

parts.note: suggests lodgings or coins from a financial bank, but means a dwelling moored beside a river bank

explanation.surface: Lodging arranged by a lender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money; it is the side of a river, where a floating home is tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel fitted out as a home is a set of living quarters lying moored alongside a riverside.

clue.text: Record of a governess left in Siam

parts.note: Anna Leonowens was the English governess at the court of Siam, as in The King and I

explanation.surface: An account kept by a governess who remained in Siam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Siam' pins down which governess: Anna, of 'Anna and the King of Siam'. 'Left' looks like 'remained' but is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: A single entry in a chronicle of yearly events; the plural is the usual form for historical records.

clue.text: I leave the head cook in charge

indicators.note: leave tells us the letter I departs from the word that follows

parts.note: a chief is a head or leader

explanation.surface: Someone resigning from the top kitchen job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I leave' reads as someone quitting; it tells you to remove I from CHIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from French chef de cuisine, the head of a kitchen.

clue.text: A criminal picked up in response to a telephone call

definitions.meaning: one who knowingly handles stolen goods, a fence

definitions.text: picked up in response to a telephone call
definitions.meaning: the handset lifted when the phone rings

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a handler of stolen property and the part of a phone held to the ear.

clue.text: Regularly visits university in county

indicators.note: in places the university letter within the county abbreviation

parts.note: Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, a county in southern England

explanation.surface: Someone often calls at a university in the shires.
explanation.walkthrough: HANTS is the usual short form of Hampshire, a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To frequent a place, like a ghost returning to the same spot.

clue.text: Circus performer

parts.note: suggests an acrobat or clown, but means a tiny insect trained for a novelty ... circus

explanation.definitionFit: Insect circuses were a fairground attraction in which tiny parasites appeared to pull carts and juggle.

clue.text: Non-playing coach attached to cricket side

indicators.note: attached to sets the coach word after the cricket side word

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
a stage, as in stagecoach, is a horse-drawn coach

explanation.surface: A trainer who does not play is linked to a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricket side' suggests a team; in cricket the off side is the half of the field the batter faces. 'Coach' is a stagecoach, not a trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of view of the audience, an actor is not performing.

clue.text: The m6 junction, of course

parts.note: the tangle of roads at Gravelly Hill on the M6 near Birmingham is nicknamed after a pasta, which is also served as a meal course

explanation.surface: An interchange on a British motorway, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: The M6 is a major British motorway; its Gravelly Hill interchange in Birmingham is famously nicknamed after a long thin pasta. 'Of course' means 'naturally' on the surface but points to a dinner course.
explanation.definitionFit: The pasta lends its name to the famous interchange, and it is eaten as one course of a meal.

clue.text: Appointment accepted by stout preacher

indicators.note: accepted by means the job word is taken inside the drink word

parts.note: stout is a dark beer, so ale stands in for it
a post is a job or appointment

explanation.surface: A heavy clergyman agrees to take up a position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' poses as an adjective describing a portly preacher, but it is a dark beer; 'accepted by' asks for the job word to sit inside the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: One of Christ's twelve disciples, sent out to spread the gospel by preaching.

clue.text: Reserve given regular role as player

parts.note: set means fixed or regular, as in a set routine
an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: An understudy is offered a permanent acting job.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something for a particular purpose is to put it aside for later.

clue.text: Overweight boy's tie pulled out

definitions.note: used here as a noun, excess weight

indicators.note: a tie pulled out of shape is disordered, so the letters of the boy's tie are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plump lad has had his necktie yanked loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulled out' rearranges BOYSTIE, the letters of 'boy's tie', the possessive S included.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition of carrying far too much body fat is the state of being too heavy.

clue.text: Squander one's stake in an investment

parts.note: to blue money is old British slang for spending it recklessly
a chip is a gambling token used as a stake

explanation.surface: Wasting one's wager on a financial venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' as a verb meaning squander (usually spelt 'blow' now) is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A share in a large, reliable company is a safe stock, named after the highest-value poker token.

clue.text: Old and bald eccentric? Could be

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of old and bald might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Is an aged hairless man peculiar? Possibly.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses OLD and BALD only; 'and' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a strange, unconventional person.

clue.text: Shaken and upset

definitions.meaning: stirred up or disturbed, as a liquid

explanation.definitionFit: The word means physically stirred and also nervously disturbed or worried.

clue.text: Act in rotation

definitions.meaning: a performer's act in a variety show

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a variety performer's slot on the bill and also a single revolution.

clue.text: Above making a bad pun about love

indicators.note: about means the letters of the reworked word go around the zero letter
bad suggests the word pun is mangled into a new order

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Superior to cracking a poor joke concerning romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' turns PUN into UPN, and 'about' puts it around O for love (nil in tennis).
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean on top of or over something.

clue.text: Goes round foreign bistro

indicators.note: foreign implies the word bistro is made strange, its letters reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone circles a restaurant abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet circles the sun in its path, so the verb means travels around.

clue.text: Jack gets this to fold up

definitions.text: Jack gets this to fold up

parts.words: Jack gets this to fold up
parts.note: put after jack, the word forms a compound verb meaning to bend double, and also names a blade that folds into its handle

explanation.surface: A man named Jack is given something so he can collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: Add the answer to 'jack' and you get a verb meaning to fold or double up, as a lorry does when it skids.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding pocket blade is named by joining the word to jack, and that compound also means to bend in two.

clue.text: Restrain one's anger?

definitions.meaning: a person's rage, as in losing it

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to moderate, as a noun a fit of rage, so it both checks and is the outburst.

clue.text: Personal column

parts.note: suggests the small-ads section of a newspaper, but means the spinal column that each person has

explanation.definitionFit: The spine is the column of vertebrae running down a body.

clue.text: Not smiling back

definitions.meaning: the rear part of a ship

explanation.definitionFit: The word means grim-faced and also the rear of a vessel.

clue.text: Simple difference of opinion, but he goes to court

parts.note: plain means simple or unadorned
a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: A straightforward disagreement, yet one party sues.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who brings a lawsuit is the one who takes a case to the judge.
